title: People v. Jugueta
summary: The Supreme Court laid down definitive guidelines on the amounts of damages to be awarded in criminal cases depending on the penalty imposed. This became the controlling case for standardizing civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages across criminal law.
doctrine: When the penalty imposed is death (reduced to reclusion perpetua): civil indemnity of P100,000, moral damages of P100,000, and exemplary damages of P100,000. When the penalty is reclusion perpetua: P75,000 each. When the penalty is reclusion temporal: P50,000 each. These amounts serve as guidelines for all criminal cases.
fullText:
PERALTA, J.:

This case provides an opportunity to lay down guidelines on the proper amounts of damages to be awarded in criminal cases.

The Court rationalizes the award of damages in criminal cases based on the penalty imposed. The amounts of civil indemnity, moral damages, and exemplary damages shall be determined by the severity of the crime and the penalty attached thereto.

These guidelines shall be applied prospectively and shall govern the award of damages in all criminal cases decided hereafter.
